title: Baked Ham
subtitle: Scales to your joint · gas mark 6
description: A whole ham baked under a flour-and-water huff paste so it steams tender, then finished with browned breadcrumbs or a glaze. Set the weight of your joint and the quantities and bake time scale to match.

source.name: Adapted from a mid-century Regulo cookery guide

ingredients.note: soaked 24h, trimmed; enter your joint's weight above
roughly 2 parts flour to 1 part water
browned, to finish (or use a glaze)

steps.text: Soak the {{ham}} in plenty of cold water for 24 hours to draw out salt, changing the water once or twice. Drain and trim neatly.
Heat the oven to gas mark 6 (200°C / 180°C fan). Mix the {{flour}} and {{water}} into a stiff paste, roll it out, and wrap the {{ham}} completely so it's sealed in.
Bake in the middle of the oven. The timer is set for your joint — about 36 minutes per pound for hams up to 3 lb, or 30 minutes per pound between 3 and 6 lb.
Lift out and let it rest until cool enough to handle. Peel off the paste and the skin.
Press {{breadcrumbs}} over the fat (or brush with your glaze) and, if you like, flash back in the hot oven for a few minutes to set. Slice and serve.

notes: The 24-hour soak assumes a traditional salted/cured ham; for a mild supermarket gammon a few hours is plenty, or skip it and just simmer-then-bake.
The flour paste (a 'huff paste') isn't for eating — it traps steam so the meat stays moist. Discard it after baking.
Gas mark 6 is about 200°C conventional / 180°C fan.
For a glaze instead of crumbs: score the fat, stud with cloves, and brush with mustard and brown sugar or honey before the final blast in the oven.
